title: Absolute cohomological dimension for a profinite family of geometric proper fibres
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E\}$, with the discrete topology for $A$ and the induced $\ell$-adic topology otherwise [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Its condensed ring uses all continuous maps from profinite sets. For a scheme $T$ put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}$, using ordinary uncompleted module-object derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] and the small-site/indexing universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal P_T$ be the intersection of all replete classes in $\mathcal A_T$ containing zero and all finite constant scalar-model constructible modules [sk-def-sfb-constructible], closed under kernels and cokernels of maps between members, extensions, and all small ambient coproducts. Extension closure means that in $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ membership of both ends implies membership of the middle. 
Let $C$ be an affine reduced zero-dimensional w-contractible scheme all of whose residue fields are separably closed [sk-def-pe-wlocal]; zero-dimensional here means that every prime of its affine coordinate ring is maximal. Let $h:Z\to C$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $e\geq0$ be an integer such that for every geometric point $\bar c:\operatorname{Spec}K\to C$, with $K$ algebraically closed, the fibre $Z_{\bar c}=Z\times_C\operatorname{Spec}K$ has topological Krull dimension at most $e$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then for every $N\in\mathcal P_Z$,
$$H^r\bigl(R\Gamma(Z_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},N)\bigr)=0\qquad(r>2e+2).$$
Here $R\Gamma$ is the ordinary right derived global-section functor of $\mathcal A_Z$, valued in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$, and $N$ is placed in degree zero. The same numerical bound works for all such $N$, including arbitrary small coproducts and kernels and cokernels between their members. No Noetherianity, finite presentation of $h$, invertibility of $\ell$, or derived completeness is assumed. The empty $C$ and empty fibres are included.

proof.text: The definition of properness says that $h$ is separated and of finite type. Fix an affine open $j:V\hookrightarrow Z$. Restrict a finite-type affine coordinate cover for $h$ to $V$, and refine by principal affine opens. This gives local finite type for $h\circ j$. Because both $V$ and $C$ are affine, this morphism is quasi-compact, so it is of finite type. Its geometric fibre is the open subspace $V_{\bar c}\subseteq Z_{\bar c}$. Dimension cannot increase on an open subspace: taking closures in the ambient space sends a strict chain of irreducible closed subsets to a strict chain, since intersecting back with the subspace recovers the original chain. Hence every geometric fibre of $V\to C$ has dimension at most the same $e$.

proof.text: For an affine open U of Z, properness over the affine base makes Z qcqs. The affine-local clause of finiteConstantStratified_zariski_locality sends each constant-model constructible generator to a constant-model constructible module on U. Put F = upperStar Lambda U.ι and P = weakSerreCoproductClosure(IsConstantModelConstructible Lambda U). The inverse-image property P.inverseImage F is replete and closed under kernels, cokernels, extensions and the prescribed small coproducts: F is exact by the existing source-library instances and preserves those coproducts by its pullback/direct-image adjunction. Apply the defining minimality of weakSerreCoproductClosure to this inverse-image property. This proves restriction of N belongs to the same closure on U without asserting closure of a cohomological vanishing class under kernels.

proof.text:
Take any $N\in\mathcal P_Z$. For each affine open $V\subseteq Z$, Step 1 supplies the finite-type affine $V\to C$ and the fibre-dimension bound $e$, while Step 2 gives $j^*N\in\mathcal P_V$. Apply the affine Artin-type estimate to obtain
$$H^qR\Gamma(V_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},j^*N)=0\qquad(q>e+2).$$
The hypotheses on the base $C$ and all coefficient topologies are unchanged. The affine input applies to this whole closure class; no replacement by completed modules is used.

proof.text: Compare the two actual ordinary module-section functors on an affine open j:U→Z. Mod.extendScalarsIsoComapInv along the invertible coefficient morphism identifies the underlying sheaf of upperStar Lambda j with abelian inverse image. upperStarIsoOpenImmersionRestriction identifies that inverse image with localization restriction, whose value at id_U is evaluation at j. These yield a natural isomorphism j^* followed by sections on U ≅ evaluation at the pro-etale object j. The exact extension by zero is left adjoint to module upperStar, so upperStar preserves injectives. The source-library rightDerivedCompIsoOfExact therefore derives this section comparison in every natural degree. The source-library homologyRightDerivedFunctorObjSingleFunctorIso identifies cohomology of unbounded derived sections on a degree-zero module with its classical right derived sections. Convert r to a natural number using r>2e+2, and apply the coefficient-independent affine-to-global input to C,Z,h,Lambda_Z,N,e,a=e+2. The local condition is Step 3 transported by the comparisons just proved; properness gives separatedness and finite type. Transport the conclusion back to the integer-degree derived-section formulation. Arithmetic identifies e+(e+2) with 2e+2. All constructions and both stated inputs allow the empty scheme.
